elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso permits Licensee to assign the Agreement in its entirety, without Licensor's consent, to an Affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits a consent-free assignment to a successor in connection with a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits a consent-free assignment to a successor in connection with an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The proviso permits a consent-free assignment to a successor in connection with a sale of all or substantially all of Licensee's assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may not assign the Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent.

elements.element: For a Vendor assignment not barred by the competitor prohibition, Customer may not unreasonably withhold its consent.
elements.evidence: Licensee's consent to a Licensor assignment is expressly stated not to be unreasonably withheld, subject to the separate absolute competitor prohibition required by the preferred position.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may assign 'in no event to a competitor of Licensee.'

elements.element: Customer's change of control must not give Vendor a termination right.
elements.evidence: Article XX states that a Change of Control of Licensee shall not give Licensor any right to terminate the Agreement or Licensee's rights or licenses.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Licensee may assign without Licensor consent to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all assets or equity.

elements.element: Customer must provide Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The consent-free successor assignment right is expressly conditioned on written notice to Licensor.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: No successor carve-out is provided for Licensor; every Licensor assignment requires Licensee's prior written consent and assignments to Licensee competitors are absolutely prohibited.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice mechanism for a Licensor assignment to a successor because Licensor has no consent-free successor assignment right.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Licensee generally may not assign the Agreement or transfer its license rights without Licensor's prior written consent, subject to the stated affiliate and successor carve-outs.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer's other assignments.
elements.evidence: Licensor's consent to Licensee's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Licensor may not assign the Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent; there is no Licensor successor carve-out.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor's other assignments.
elements.evidence: Although the clause generally says Licensee's consent may not be unreasonably withheld, it categorically prohibits every assignment to a Licensee competitor. That unconditional prohibition overrides the reasonableness standard for that class of other assignments.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred position: Licensee receives the required affiliate and transaction-successor carve-outs, Licensor assignments require reasonable Licensee consent and are barred to competitors, and Licensee change of control creates no Licensor termination right. The fallback is not independently satisfied because Licensor receives no successor assignment right on written notice, and the absolute competitor bar qualifies the fallback's otherwise mutual reasonableness standard. The redline is not minimal because it also adds reorganization and equity-sale carve-outs, notice duties, a prohibition on suspension and repricing, and 'conditioned or delayed' language beyond what is needed for the preferred position. It otherwise preserves the intended allocation without an operative commercial contradiction. Drafting quality is materially impaired by the uncorrected run-on text ('Section Subject'), inconsistent section references, and awkward placement of the retained assignment language.
